newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Applied Materials sees buy benefits.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Applied Materials sees buy benefits.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc, the U.S. company which makes the equipment that produces semiconductors, said two recent acquisitions should generate a billion dollars worth of business early in the next century.
In January this year Applied Materials, from Santa Clara, California, bought Opal Inc of the U.S. for $175 million, and Orbot Instruments Ltd of Yavne, Israel for $110 million.
Both companies operate in the process control and diagnostics market.

"The process control and diagnostics market is a rapidly growing market which had sales of $1.2 billion in 1996, and will grow to over $3 billion by 2001," James Morgan, Applied Materials' chairman said.

"We made those two acquisitions earlier this year and it's a big opportunity for us. We should be able to build a billion dollar business or more out of that sub-sector of the market," Morgan told Reuters in an interview.
Morgan said Opal and Orbot had sales of about $120 million in 1996.
Most of Applied Materials' business comes from providing the technology for companies like Intel Corp, Motorola Inc, and Siemens AG to make semiconductors.
In 1996, Applied Materials had sales of $4.14 billion.

Morgan said that Applied Materials prospects were exciting because of the increasing semiconductor content found in electronic devices. About 20 percent of the value of electronic devices now reflected chips, up from three percent 20 years ago.

Morgan quoted research from U.S. high-technology consultancy Dataquest, which estimated that the world wide business of wafer fabrication capital equipment would rise to $38 billion by 2002 from $16 billion in 1997.
"We consider ourselves to be the leader in that business and feel we can gain share and leverage our global position in the future," Morgan said.
